deep.reconstruction:
Notation: ∫1/z^μ (1/y^ν) denotes Euler's double sum S(μ,ν) = Σ_{z≥1} z^{-μ} Σ_{y=1}^{z} y^{-ν}. This is a non-strict double zeta value, ζ(μ,ν)+ζ(μ+ν) in modern strict notation. ∫1/z^m denotes ζ(m).

§10. Euler looks back at the expansions from his 'second method' (previous page). These write ζ(m)ζ(n) − ζ(m+n), split according to the parity of m and n, as linear combinations of products ζ(a)ζ(b) and double sums S(μ,ν). He observes that every S(μ,ν) appearing has μ+ν = m+n. He therefore proposes to arrange the investigation in 'ordines' by the value of m+n; in modern terms this is grading by weight.

He pairs each order with the 'first method' theorem S(m,n)+S(n,m) = ζ(m)ζ(n)+ζ(m+n). This is the harmonic (stuffle) product written for non-strict sums, with the diagonal counted twice. Combining the two kinds of relation in each weight should let him evaluate the individual S(μ,ν). Since m,n ≥ 1, the orders are weight 2, 3, 4, and so on. Because ζ(1) is infinite, any convergent sum must come out with the divergence cancelled.

§11, weight 2. Only (1,1) is possible. The second method turns ζ(1)² − ζ(2) into S(1,1)+S(1,1) = 2S(1,1). The first method gives 2S(1,1) = ζ(1)² + ζ(2). On the next page Euler notes the apparent contradiction (a discrepancy of 2ζ(2)). He dismisses it on the grounds that ζ(2) is negligible against the infinite ζ(1)², so nothing can be concluded in weight 2.

Weight 3 (next page) gives S(2,1) = 2ζ(3), i.e. ζ(2,1) = ζ(3).
errors: No error on this page itself. The weight-2 'resolution' ζ(1)²−ζ(2) = 2S(1,1) is a formal manipulation of divergent series and genuinely conflicts with the stuffle identity, which holds exactly for truncated sums: Σ_{y≤z≤N} 1/(yz) = (H_N² + H_N^{(2)})/2. Euler correctly refuses to draw conclusions from it.

ideas.what: Non-strict double sums S(m,n) = Σ_z z^{-m} H_z^{(n)} as objects of study
ideas.modern_name: double zeta values / linear Euler sums

ideas.what: Organizing relations by μ+ν = m+n, noting all relations are homogeneous in this sum
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler implicitly; formalized by Zagier, Goncharov, Hoffman (1990s)

ideas.what: Divergent ζ(1) must drop out for convergent sums; weight-2 relations rejected because of divergence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara–Kaneko–Zagier (2006) for systematic regularized double shuffle

missed.claim: In weight 2, Euler's two methods (partial-fraction/'shuffle-like' versus harmonic product) give conflicting values of the divergent S(1,1), differing by a ζ(2) term. This is an early instance of the phenomenon that shuffle- and stuffle-regularizations of divergent MZVs differ by explicit ζ(2)-type corrections, the content of the IKZ comparison map ρ. Histories credit Euler with double zeta values and ζ(2,1)=ζ(3), but I am unsure whether this specific weight-2 conflict has been singled out as a precursor of regularized double shuffle.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical precursor of the regularization discrepancy in double shuffle theory; mainly of historiographical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: The weight grading and the stuffle relation in E477 are well known and credited to Euler. The only mildly notable point is the explicit weight-2 inconsistency between methods, an anticipation of regularization issues; it is probably known to MZV historians.
